newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Life Sciences shares up on Thermo bid.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Life Sciences shares up on Thermo bid.

text.p: Acquisitive U.S. firm Thermo Instrument Systems Inc made an agreed 235.9 million pounds ($392 million) offer for Britain's Life Sciences International Plc on Tuesday, sending shares in the scientific equipment producer romping ahead by 44 percent.

The 135 pence per share cash offer is Thermo's biggest acquisition yet and follows last year's purchase of British pharmaceutical company Fisons Plc's worldwide scientific instruments division for 202 million pounds.

Thermo said Life Sciences' manufacturing, distribution and service base will help it extend its product offerings into new markets such as clinical laboratory equipment and will enhance its presence in the bio-analytical instrumentation marketplace.

Riccardo Pigliucci, chief executive of Life Sciences, told Reuters, "Thermo is now expanding into the laboratory equipment markets and clinical markets and is looking at Life Sciences as the seed company to expand in that area."

Thermo, which is 82 percent owned by Thermo Electron Corp, develops, manufactures, and markets instruments used to detect and measure air pollution, radioactivity, complex chemical compounds, toxic metals and other elements.

Life Sciences intends to declare a second interim dividend, in place of any final dividend, for the year ended December 31, 1996 of 3.0 pence per share. It also expects profit before tax and exceptional items for the year ended December 31, 1996 to be around 27.0 million pounds from 24.0 million pounds in 1995.

The offer together with the second interim dividend represents a premium of around 49 percent to Life Sciences' closing share price on Monday. By 1152 GMT, shares in Life Sciences had roared ahead 40-1/2 pence to stand at 133 pence.

Thermo, which has a market capitalisation of around 3.2 billion dollars, said that the acquisition will be financed from its cash resources and expects the purchase to enhance its earnings straight away.
The U.S. company also revealed that it will continue to keep an eye on possible further acquisitions.

"We are in discussion with a number of companies all the time, some in Europe, some in the U.S, some in the Far East," Earl Lewis, executive vice president and chief operating officer of Thermo Instruments told Reuters.
"At any point in time there are anywhere up to 30 or 40 companies that we are actively watching." ($1=.6021 Pound)
